title: Holistic model throughput + tail-latency benchmarker
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build and maintain a lightweight, deterministic benchmark harness that measures both tokens-per-second throughput and tail latency (p95/p99) across our core production models. The harness must support: reproducible synthetic workloads, KV-cache warm/cold scenarios, variable sequence lengths, multi-replica stress, and automated regression detection integrated with CI. Output artifacts should include time-series metrics, per-run baselines, and a small HTML dashboard for quick investigation. Goal is to detect regressions before customer impact and provide actionable root-cause signals (model/kernel/hardware/packing).
tasks: Design canonical workload profiles (chat-like short-turns, long-form generation, embeddings-batching).
Implement deterministic request generator with configurable seed, seq_len distribution, and prefix/KV warmup steps.
Add KV-cache warm/cold toggles and record cache hit curves per run.
Instrument p95 and p99 tracking and provide percentile bucketing for token-level latency.
Integrate benchmark runs into CI (nightly and on-runtime-rollouts) with regression thresholds and automatic issue filing.
Persist per-model baselines in CloudStorage and expose diffs in a lightweight dashboard (static HTML + JSON).
Create a small set of attack scenarios for autoscaler/steady-state verification (burst + sustained load).
Document running instructions and developer guide; include troubleshooting checklist for false positives.

decision_log: Adopt JSON-lines artifacts and S3 storage for run results to keep dashboard ingestion simple.
Use deterministic synthetic prompts rather than live traffic to avoid PII exposure and make runs faster and repeatable.
Regression detection will use moving-median baseline + hysteresis window to reduce false positives from infra noise.
